local_checks.invariant: The pathname passed to the self-fetch must stay a same-origin path (no protocol-relative or backslash forms).
local_checks.result: The route builds pathname as '/' + path.join('/') with no normalization (route.ts:34-35). Segments that decode to '//evil.example', ['', 'evil.example'] or '\\evil.example' produce '///evil.example', '//evil.example' and '/\\evil.example'. WHATWG new URL(pathname, base) resolves all three to https://evil.example/, while string concatenation stays same-origin. Which join accept-md-runtime@5.0.2 uses is unknown because the package is absent.

local_checks.invariant: Shared caches (in-process Map and CDN s-maxage) must key on every input that changes the response.
local_checks.result: The response is public, s-maxage=60 with Vary: Accept only (route.ts:50-56; next.config.mjs:33-39 adds Vary: Accept to all paths). The 250-entry in-process markdownCache is shared across all requests (route.ts:8,44), and its key is computed inside accept-md-runtime, which is not present. Host and forwarded headers are not in Vary. If the origin or pathname can be steered, the cached markdown could be served to other visitors. This cannot be decided from source.

local_checks.invariant: A markdown self-fetch must never re-enter the accept-md rewrite. Each anonymous request must cause at most one extra origin render.
local_checks.result: The route removes only the `accept` header before the self-fetch (route.ts:36-37). That stops loops through the Accept-header rewrite (next.config.mjs:19-29). The pathname is rebuilt from the decoded path segments (route.ts:34-35) and fetched against request.nextUrl.origin (route.ts:42). If a pathname ends in `.md`, the self-fetch is rewritten back into accept-md with one `.md` removed. So `/a.md.md...md` with k suffixes becomes a chain of k nested public-origin invocations, all held open at once. The only limit is URL length. local_checks.invariant: The built-in /_next/image optimizer should accept only the finite set of remote source URLs the site renders, so anonymous visitors cannot create unlimited distinct optimizer jobs or cache entries.
local_checks.result: next.config.mjs:47-54 limits remote sources to https://www.google.com with pathname /s2/favicons. It sets no 'search' constraint, so the domain/domain_url/sz query values are free. Legitimate uses (components/tool-parts.tsx:35, lib/portfolio-data.ts:91) put a visitor-invisible but arbitrary-looking domain into the query. Each one triggers an upstream fetch, a sharp transform, and a new optimizer-cache entry, which may count as a billable Vercel source image. Per-request work is small because favicons are tiny and widths and qualities come from the framework allowlist, so the cost lies in cardinality and spend, not in per-request amplification. Framework defaults and Vercel billing are not visible here. Recorded as needs_validation.
